title: Transitivity of canonically normalized coefficient mates on sheaf topoi
statement:
Let $h:\mathscr X\to\mathscr Y$ be a morphism of sheaf topoi presented by sites small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism, def-weil-size-convention]. Fix maps of commutative ring sheaves $R_Y\xrightarrow a S_Y\xrightarrow b T_Y$, and take their inverse images on $\mathscr X$. Use ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], K-flat derived scalar extensions $E_{S/R,W},E_{T/S,W},E_{T/R,W}$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and the derived adjunctions $L_A=h_A^*\dashv G_A=Rh_{*,A}$ canonically derived from the ordinary module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], for $A=R,S,T$.
For each coefficient map $A\to B$ define $\gamma^{B/A}_K:E_{B/A,Y}G_AK\to G_BE_{B/A,X}K$ to be the adjunct of the canonical balanced comparison $L_BE_{B/A,Y}G_AK\cong E_{B/A,X}L_AG_AK$ followed by scalar extension of $\varepsilon_{A,K}$ [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$\beta_W:E_{T/S,W}E_{S/R,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{T/R,W}$$
specified on flat-term K-flat representatives by $t\otimes s\otimes p\mapsto t b(s)\otimes p$, with inverse $t\otimes p\mapsto t\otimes1\otimes p$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. They intertwine the composite pullback/scalar balancing maps with the balancing map for $R\to T$, preserving the scalar-unit normalization $p\mapsto1\otimes p$. For every $K\in D(R_X)$, composition right to left satisfies
$$\gamma^{T/R}_K\circ\beta_{Y,G_RK}=G_T(\beta_{X,K})\circ\gamma^{T/S}_{E_{S/R,X}K}\circ E_{T/S,Y}(\gamma^{S/R}_K).$$
This is equality of the specified derived morphisms with their specified geometric counits; neither coefficient map is assumed flat and neither comparison is assumed invertible.

proof.text: The normalized unit equation extends from flat-term K-flat resolving complexes to every complex by the general unit_all localization argument. This is needed because the successive-quotient theorem existentially chooses its models and cannot directly supply isomorphisms for the six models fixed in this statement. The proof constructs comparisons for those fixed models explicitly.

proof.text: Construct the literal identity-on-sections restriction-composition isomorphism, as in successive derived quotient normalization, and its exact derived compositor. Construct the ordinary and derived scalar-tower isomorphisms by uniqueness of left adjoints to the composed restriction adjunction. Their unit identities determine the pure-tensor formulas: the forward map sends t tensor (s tensor x) to t b(s) tensor x, and the inverse inserts 1. The existing ScalarPullback.pure_smul_one lemma and scalar insertion suffice; all scalar factors have degree zero.

proof.text: Prove the derived representative identity by applying the Hom bijection of the composite scalar adjunction. The universal cochain comparison transposes to the ordinary unit on every cochain complex, by the preceding unit equation. Transpose the two comparisons in succession and use the exact restriction-compositor factorization. This proves the representative formula for the specified tower isomorphism. Scalar extension is ringed pullback on the identity topos, so the K-flat pullback theorem supplies the intermediate K-flat and flat-term conditions and hence invertibility of the second model comparison.

proof.text: Check the ordinary restriction-action square after applying the faithful underlying-sheaf functor. The formula for each action is the underlying inverse-image comparison followed by the inverse comparison for the target ring; the middle comparisons cancel, and naturality supplies the restriction compositor. Apply exactSquare_comp_forward to derive this equality for the exact restriction and inverse-image functors. This uses exact localization of the restriction square rather than descent of arbitrary words of nonexact scalar extensions.

proof.text: The single-map scalar-normalization theorem supplies an invertible coefficient mate for some scalar adjunctions. Changing those adjunctions conjugates the inverse mate by the canonical invertible left-adjoint identifications, as follows from the mateEquiv conjugation rules; hence the specified coefficient mates are invertible too. Define balancing as the inverse of each specified coefficient mate. Mate the derived restriction-action square using mateEquiv_hcomp and the conjugation rules. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies the resulting composition comparison with the tower isomorphism already normalized above. Cancel only the invertible coefficient balancing maps to obtain the required balancing square.

proof.text: Use the actual geometric adjunctions canonically derived from the given ordinary module adjunctions. The pasted-mates counit-normalization theorem computes the counit transpose of the successive geometric mates followed by beta_X. Transpose the direct mate preceded by beta_Y, apply the balancing square, and use naturality of beta_X at the R-counit. The transposes agree, so injectivity of the Hom equivalence proves the final equality. No geometric right mate is inverted.
